newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra attacks aid group for activist politics.
newsitem.headline: Canberra attacks aid group for activist politics.

text.p: A senior member of the Australian government on Tuesday attacked aid groups for their part in urging Britain to tackle Prime Minister John Howard on Aboriginal issues during his visit there this month.

Assistant Foreign Affairs Minister Andrew Thomson said aid agency Community Aid Abroad had forgotten its place when it joined with union and religious leaders to urge British Prime Minister Tony Blair to discuss native title issues with Howard.

"Aid agencies who lapse into political campaigns designed to cause people overseas to hate Australia are doing appalling damage to the fund-raising efforts of decent aid agencies," Thomson said in a statement.
Thomson called on Community Aid Abroad to focus on genuine aid and to stay away from activist politics.
"It gives the wrong impression to corporate and individual donors that aid agencies are out to blacken Australia's good name," he said.
Community Aid Abroad joined with the other groups to sign a letter due to be published in The Times of London on Tuesday, in which Blair was asked to intervene on the native title issue.

Native title laws were introduced by the former Labor government three years ago, but became an important political issue when the High Court decided last December that land leased to farmers could be liable to Aboriginal claim.
Howard has developed a 10-point plan aimed at satisfying both Aborigines and farmers on land rights, but the signatories to the letter have labelled the plan as inadequate.
Howard left Canberra on Tuesday for a 16-day visit to London, Washington and New York, where he will concentrate on forging personal ties with Blair and U.S. President Bill Clinton.
The prime minister has dismissed the letter as a stunt.
